title: OU softball sets fall attendance record in 35-0 rout behind Nelly McEnroe-Marinas & Co. - NewsBreak
text:
By Colton Sulley ,
7 hours ago
NORMAN — OU softball routed Oklahoma Christian 35-0 in a fall exhibition game Wednesday night at Love’s Field.
The Sooners belted 10 home runs in the win.
LSU transfer and former All-SEC pitcher Sydney Berzon started for the Sooners, retiring all six Eagles she faced. She allowed zero hits in two innings of work with no strikeouts.
Berzon is having a nice fall thus far after ending her Tigers career with a 2.02 ERA and 416 strikeouts in 486 ⅓ innings and is expected to be OU’s ace in the spring. She recorded 13 shutouts and ranks No. 3 all-time with nine saves in LSU’s program history.
“Sydney Berzon is going to get better than she is right now, and I know that she is in a new program with a new coach, with a new training staff,” OU coach Patty Gasso said.
“We're really working hard to give her what she needs and have the right people working for her. When that happens, and she's totally committed to the rehab side of things and working in the training room, but when that happens, you're going to see something.
“She's going to become what she always thought she could become, and what's going to be wonderful about it, it's happening here at Oklahoma her senior year. So I'm just glad we're all going to be here to witness it.”
Sophomore left-hander Audrey Lowry allowed one hit and walked one batter in two innings. Lowry is fresh off a freshman campaign with the Sooners, in which she finished with a 3.09 earned run average.
Sophomore Riley Zache relieved Lowry in the fifth, striking out three, allowing one hit and two walks in two innings. Senior left-hander Kierston Deal struck out three in two innings. Miali Guachino finished it off, striking out five of the six hitters she faced with no hits allowed.
Here are some takeaways from the Sooners’ fall exhibition:

Nelly McEnroe-Marinas goes yard twice Redshirt sophomore infielder Nelly McEnroe-Marinas finished 4-for-4 at the plate with two home runs, a triple and a walk on Wednesday.
McEnroe-Marinas homered in the fifth and sixth and also finished with six RBIs.
“I feel a lot more comfortable,” McEnroe-Marinas said. “It's more so because I have 100% faith and trust in my team and knowing that no pressure is on me because they'll pick me up no matter what. And I feel like that kind of goes with our team camaraderie and just being able to pick each other up and having each other's backs no matter what.”
McEnroe-Marinas was a double away from hitting for the cycle.
“It's been a blessing being able to experience what I have in my last few years, but also just knowing that this team definitely has my back,” McEnroe-Marinas said.
Sooners combine for 23 runs in third, fourth, fifth innings OU showed its superiority in the third, fourth and fifth innings.
The Sooners’ bats got hot, beginning with a solo home run from freshman Kendall Wells to lead off the third. Five OU batters walked in the third, leading to six more runs.
“We're starting to get better now,” Gasso said. “They're hitting a lot more. They're spending time with JT, They're figuring out their swing. There's just a chase going on here. Everybody is chasing each other, and so you better run fast, or someone's going to pass you, someone's going to get you.
Kasidi Pickering, who hit 18 home runs last spring, belted one to right center field to lead off the fourth. From there, Chaney Helton homered to right field, Ailana Agbayani and Abby Dayton each smacked RBI-triples and Tia Milloy crushed a two-run home run in the fourth.
In the fifth, the Sooners added nine runs, including a three-run home run from Ella Parker.
Get to know freshman Kendall Wells Wells, a true freshman from Bogart, Georgia, is a player to watch in the spring.
She finished with two home runs in the blowout exhibition. Her home run was her fourth in three fall ball games.
“Easy, just looks easy,” Gasso said. “She just has a presence at the plate, that if I was a pitcher, I would think I got to be very careful here, and if you're making a pitcher think that just by the way you look at the plate, you've won. She always gets her swing off. So it's been really impressive.”
A right-handed-hitting catcher from North Oconee High School, Wells produced 127 hits, 55 home runs,184 RBIs, 148 walks, 162 runs scored and 62 stolen bases during her prep career.
“It’s definitely been a really cool experience,” Wells said. “It’s really helpful and cool to be in this environment so early in my career. To be playing in front of 2,800 fans in the fall is not something that all freshmen get to experience, so I think that’s really cool helping all of us freshmen out a lot being able to experience this early on.
“But we have great teammates by our side that are there and have been in this situation before and help us get through it.”
OU softball fall scrimmage draws nearly 3,000 fans The lines outside Gate 2 of Love’s Field stretched all the way to Imhoff Road on a Wednesday night in October.
For a fall softball exhibition game.
The 2,837 fans in attendance set a new fall game attendance record.
“First, the crowd was amazing,” Gasso said. “I don't think we expected anything like that so just a shout out to OU softball fans who came out and spent the evening with us, and they were great. And it was a fun atmosphere.
“I don't know anybody else that's bringing in 2,800 for their fall games so we're really excited about that. It really does help us, and especially our young players, feel the atmosphere, because it's not easy.”
Next up, the Sooners play their second intrasquad Battle Series game at 6:30 p.m. on Friday.
